title: KVCache eviction regression log
summary: Working notes tracing a recent latency regression that correlated with higher KV-cache eviction rates. Includes dashboard observations, bisect plan, microbenchmark results, and suggested instrumentation to improve detection and automatic triage.
body:
Context:
We started seeing intermittent 95th/99th p95 spikes in text-generation paths on the rtx-pool during the 2024-09-14 canary window. Root signal in the alert: token-latency-surge (threshold 2.1x baseline) triggered across multiple models at once. Initial blamestack pointed to increased upstream request spread, but the profile snapshots show a pattern: simultaneous rise in KV cache evictions and a corresponding increase in top-of-stack attention re-computation time.

High-level hypothesis:
When KV-cache eviction rate increases (shortened cache TTL or memory pressure), the serving runtime spends more cycles reloading prefix KV and redoing attention recompute for long-context requests. This disproportionately impacts tail latency because large-context requests are less frequent but expensive when cache is cold. The canary had a subtle infra change that reduced per-container page cache reservation (OOM tuning), pushing working sets a hair over threshold for some instance types.

What we observed (dashboards & quick metrics):
- Grafana panel 'kvcache/evictions_per_min' shows a 3-5x step up starting 2024-09-14 02:30 UTC on canary nodes (query: sum by(node) (rate(kvcache_evictions_total[5m]))).
- Tail latency (p99-token-latency) correlates with evictions with a lag of ~20–40s on several spikes.
- CPU cycles in the attention kernel per-token increased ~18% on sampled traces where evictions count > 0 for that session.
- Microbench harness reproduced the spike when we artificially forced KV-cache misses on sequences >1024 tokens.

Reproduction steps used in the lab:
1) Run microbench-gen.py with a mixture of short (64) and long (2048) sequences at ramped concurrency.
2) Toggle the evict flag in the runtime (runtime.conf:kvcache.force_eviction=true) and observe p95/p99 deltas.
3) Collect per-request trace (trace-id header) and map trace to kvcache.metrics.
4) Compare canary vs baseline images (image tags: canary-2024-09-12 vs baseline-2024-08-30).

Key tracing snippets (observed):
- Requests where kvcache.evictions > 0: attention.recompute_ms median 56ms vs 28ms with evictions == 0.
- Memory allocation churn increases shortly after eviction events (heap allocs + transient buffers).

Bisect plan & experiments executed:
- Step A: Isolate infra variable: rollback the page-cache tuning change on a subset of canary instances. Result: evictions drop and p99 returns near baseline for that subset.
- Step B: Isolate runtime change: deploy baseline runtime with canary infra; evictions persist — suggests infra is primary driver.
- Step C: Stress test with baseline infra but upgraded runtime kernel selection (PR #642). Minor improvements in burst handling but not enough alone.

Canary comparison methodology used:
- Use deterministic workload (microbench v2) with fixed seed, two buckets: 90% short / 10% long. Run 30-minute windows on canary vs baseline.
- Capture: per-token latency distribution, kvcache.evictions per-session, attention.kernel-ms histogram, and GC/paging counters.
- Do 5 independent runs per variant and report median and IQR for p95/p99.

Benchmarks & numbers (abridged):
- Baseline: p95 token latency = 12ms, p99 = 28ms, evictions per 5m = 1.1
- Canary (with page-cache change): p95 = 13ms, p99 = 42ms, evictions per 5m = 4.6
- Canary + kvcache eviction mitigation (runtime flag): p95 = 12.5ms, p99 = 32ms, evictions per 5m = 2.0

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Rollback page-cache tuning on affected AZs (reduced burst evictions).
- Added short-term config: kvcache.max_evict_per_min = 10 to throttle accidental mass evictions during high churn.
- Enabled per-container eviction alarm in alerting stack (new alert: evictions-rate-high-5m).

Instrumentation & detection improvements recommended:
1) Add per-request kvcache.touch_count and kvcache.eviction_reason to structured traces (so triage can differentiate policy vs memory-pressure evictions).
2) Emit a summarized trace tag when a request sees >0 evictions during lifetime (makes Grafana pivoting simpler).
3) Add heatmap panel that cross-slices node.memory.used, page-cache settings, and eviction spikes (we already added a provisional panel at linked_artifacts[1]).
4) Add a canary-specific comparative dashboard widget that automatically overlays baseline vs canary p99 and eviction rates for the last 1h.

Open questions & follow-ups:
- Why did the page-cache tuning change cause a >3x eviction rate on this particular GPU instance family? Need infra deeper dive (SRE + infra kernel logs).
- Are there workload patterns (prompt batching, long-conversation demos) that amplify the effect? We should run customer-like traces from the replay bucket.
- Is our current eviction policy optimal for multi-tenant containers? Consider per-tenant quotas or soft pinning of long-context sessions.

Next action items (owners):
- Maya: finalize the microbench reproduction script and check it into eng-serving-runtime/tools (due 2024-09-22).
- Diego: coordinate kernel/oom tuning rollback and get kernel logs for the affected window (JIRA-ENG-1729).
- Priya: instrument trace schema additions and add kvcache tags to span format (PR draft 642 referenced).
- Alex: update Grafana panels and wire an automated canary overlay (dashboard id abc123).

Notes to self / informal observations:
- We are seeing an interesting non-linear effect: small increases in eviction rate cause outsized p99 movement because a single long-context request can cascade — it pulls back a lot of prefixes from storage and temporarily blocks other concurrent requests on the same worker.
- Triage playbook suggestion: when evictions spike, quickly correlate with node-level memory metrics and page-cache changes before blaming runtime.
- This doc is a snapshot — keep evolving as infra audit log arrives.

Attachments / snippets:
- microbench invocation: python microbench-gen.py --seed 9843 --short 0.9 --long 0.1 --duration 1800 --trace
- Grafana quicklink: https://grafana.redwood-internal.com/d/abc123/kvcache-heatmap
- Repro PR (runtime flags): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/642
